Hypemesis Gravidarum?!   A more common term, in pregnant women it is more frequently referred to as "morning sickness".
The sudden onset and severity of it make it an extremely distressing condition.
Every pregnancy should include an element of morning sickness. As long as your baby is healthy, the sick symptom is most commonly associated with the fetus growing inside her for a long period of time before coming to fruition around six weeks after conception. And because your body is still producing those chemicals that make you feel nauseous, pregnant women tend to stay home from work and stay well out of restaurants until the nausea subsides.
Unfortunately, more severe cases can lead to dehydration, extreme hunger, and high levels of nausea throughout the day on constant occasions. This combination of problems is often enough to make a woman lose the will to continue eating, even if she craves certain foods or simply to avoid possible danger to herself.
